Transitive dependencies and third normal form

Unit 2 · Week 3 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the normalisation chapter, normalisation-workbook.md, normalisation-answers.md and the normalisation-pack.zip stage datasets. Use fictional data on paper or in a school-approved spreadsheet. No SQL setup or student account is required. Keep original copies. Suggested 55-minute timings are flexible. Explained answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Transitive dependencies and third normal form

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the reservation extension of the equipment desk. These are reservation requests, not issued loans. Keep the earlier Loan datasets unchanged. All activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

2. The remaining dependency chain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and partner explanation

Category should store CategoryName with CategoryID. This is the chain left in the 2NF Equipment table. We remove the dependency through a non-key attribute to reach this example’s intended 3NF design under the supplied dependencies. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

3. A category fact gets its own home

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

Description abbreviates EquipmentDescription in this summary. Create Category, move CategoryName out of Equipment, and keep CategoryID in Equipment as the reference. CategoryID determines CategoryName. The EquipmentID primary key and original item facts remain. Show Category C01 as Imaging. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

4. Four tables, defined responsibilities

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Prediction and teacher model

ReservationDate is the full date-field name. BorrowerLabel stays in Borrower, EquipmentDescription in Equipment, CategoryName in Category and ReservationStatus in Reservation. The table count does not establish a normal form. Under the stated dependencies, these tables remove the partial and transitive dependencies demonstrated here. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

5. A reconstructed request

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Start with the whole composite key to find the request. Then match identifiers to recover the descriptive facts. This reconstructs the original 1NF row. Compare B002/E01/1 May: Learner B and Requested, while the same equipment/category facts remain. Competing requests are allowed by the exercise rules. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

6. All six requests must survive

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 7–10. Final counts: 3 borrowers, 3 categories, 3 items and 6 reservations. Match IDs, not descriptions. Compare the reconstructed set of eight-field rows with the original 1NF CSV, regardless of row order. New unused equipment can exist, descriptions update once per item, and deleting a reservation need not delete item facts. Constraints and deliberate deletion policies still matter. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

7. A repeated foreign key

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. The repeated FK represents distinct requests. The descriptive Camera fact belongs once with the Equipment record. Deleting reservation rows merely to remove repeated E01 values would lose legitimate events. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.

8. A limit of normalisation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

No. Normalisation organises dependencies. Validation checks permitted forms and values, while factual accuracy requires appropriate evidence and checks. Approval/availability and conflicting confirmations also need separate rules. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#normalisation.
